{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOLEgSIs8AAAABZc9CLQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm7fazhDEK84", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm7fa", "number": 31, "title": "Correct existing WebXR event handlers and event constructors", "body": "## Problem

At `dev` revision `2b92ea462cb379c35ebb4c79777f40e3544891ba`, `XREventTarget._emit()` invokes property handlers after `dispatchEvent()` returns. Consequently, direct dispatch misses those handlers, registration order is wrong, `currentTarget` is cleared, and immediate propagation and handler-return cancellation are not integrated with dispatch.

The three existing event constructors accept invalid interface members, expose writable fields, and freeze caller-owned arrays. `XRInputSourcesChangeEvent` also incorrectly inherits from `XRSessionEvent`. These defects affect application input and session-lifecycle consumers. See [runtime.ts](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/2b92ea462cb379c35ebb4c79777f40e3544891ba/src/polyfill/api/runtime.ts#L22).

## Expected outcome

Existing XRSystem/XRSession property handlers participate in ordinary DOM dispatch. The three implemented event classes provide converted, independent, readonly event data with correct inheritance. Preserve real input-frame lifetime and shutdown behavior.

This core behavior requires no feature descriptor. Cover Quest 3 `immersive-vr`, Quest 3 MR and Android `immersive-ar`, plus inline sessions. Quest supplies controller select/squeeze actions; Android supplies transient touchscreen select actions; inline sessions must not acquire simulated immersive input merely through synthetic dispatch.

## Context

Start from and target `dev`. Inspect `runtime.ts`, the existing interface-brand/conversion helpers, `CustomWebXRPolyfill.ts`, `tests/conformance.ts`, `tests/input-lifecycle.ts`, and `tests/browser-smoke.ts`. The existing shared registry covers frames/spaces/joints; session and input-source validation needs appropriate allocation evidence rather than realm-local `instanceof` alone.

Use the fixed [Device CRD §12](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CRD-webxr-20260609/#events), supporting [HTML revision b342939](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/b342939ba3b7e40041655fb926f6e41b54fe47ef/source) event-handler algorithms, and [WebIDL revision 622910c](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/blob/622910c67c724e362f71e8255a0380bade261acb/index.bs). Adapt relevant assertions from [WPT e185958](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/tree/e1859580b5fcf74940a18d2f783296b4961035e3): `event-handler-spec-example.window.js`, `event-handler-removal.window.js`, `event-handler-processing-algorithm.html`, `interfaces/webxr.idl`, and `webxr/xrFrame_lifetime.https.html`. HTML-element content attributes are outside this XR-target adaptation.

All 30 returned Issues/PRs are closed, with no dedicated event-contract task. [Issue #11's outcome](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/issues/11#issuecomment-6203709987) explicitly retained broader WebIDL gaps. [PR #30](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/pull/30) reports a passing Chromium browser suite, including an existing throwing-handler regression; that does not establish the new dispatch/constructor cases. No evaluator tests were run.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement dispatch-integrated accessors for `ondevicechange` and existing session handlers: `onend`, `onvisibilitychange`, `oninputsourceschange`, `onselectstart`, `onselect`, `onselectend`, `onsqueezestart`, `onsqueeze`, and `onsqueezeend`. Verify initial null, registration position, replacement without repositioning, null removal and reactivation. Follow EventHandler conversion: primitives become null; non-callable objects retain identity and registration position without invoking `handleEvent`.
- [ ] Verify direct `dispatchEvent()` and emulator-generated delivery invoke each handler once, with the correct receiver, target, currentTarget and event phase. Test `stopImmediatePropagation()` before and within the property handler. Returning false cancels a cancelable synthetic event and produces the corresponding dispatch return value. Throwing handlers report their exception once, permit subsequent listeners, and do not escape dispatch or stop XR processing.
- [ ] Convert both required constructor arguments for `XRSessionEvent`, `XRInputSourceEvent`, and `XRInputSourcesChangeEvent`: DOMString type, inherited EventInit defaults, required interface members and iterable input-source sequences. Missing/undefined required members, null interfaces, invalid sequence elements and noniterables throw synchronous TypeError. Read inherited dictionary members once in base-to-derived, lexicographic order; propagate getter/iterator exceptions without freezing caller data.
- [ ] Give all three classes their specified direct Event inheritance. Expose their declared attributes as branded readonly prototype accessors with stable object identity. Change-event arrays must be frozen independent snapshots, preserving order, duplicates and source identities while leaving caller arrays and sources mutable. Test subsequent caller mutation and assignment attempts.
- [ ] Accept genuine interface values from separately injected same-origin iframe and opener-linked popup realms; reject prototype forgeries and interface proxies. Constructors must not invent session-ownership, matching-session, active-frame or live-session prerequisites. Constructing or dispatching synthetic events must not activate retained frames or perform virtual input/session actions.
- [ ] Exercise real Quest select/squeeze and Android transient select delivery through both listener styles. Pose reads remain usable during live input dispatch, event-frame `getViewerPose()` rejects with InvalidStateError, and retained event frames reject pose access afterward, including after handler exceptions. Preserve source-change ordering and asynchronous, single end-event delivery with cleanup complete.
- [ ] Integrate focused assertions into the existing browser runner for all three immersive configurations and inline coverage. Record adapted WPT paths/revision and any normative differences. The Coordinator runs `npm run build`, `npm run test:browser`, and `git diff --check`; record browser/version, tested revision, outcomes, failures, skips and unperformed checks. These are implementation-stage checks, not an additional graph-owned rerun or independent AI re-review.
- [ ] Update the packaged polyfill and versioned API inventory accurately. If an AI-authored requirement is mistaken, retain its original assumption, correction, pinned primary source and rationale in the Issue/PR. Apply evidence-backed corrections without human approval or independent AI re-review; preserve the goal and meaningful acceptance rather than weakening requirements around failures.

## Optional validation

A focused consumer check using [Three.js r186 WebXRManager](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/9b4a2ac29c63ccb43fd51c5661f2f873ac2c39b8/src/renderers/webxr/WebXRManager.js) may corroborate input-frame consumption and source-change/end cleanup. Distinguish custom fixtures from unmodified official-example execution. Missing event interfaces, unfinished modules and broader Firefox/application coverage remain separate goal work.

## Required post-merge verification

None required.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WebXR API compatibility goal for
Quest 3 VR/MR and Android AR. Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance
criteria when primary specifications or measured evidence establish the correction.
Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.
